description: Prefix caching: chained block hashes, hits and misses, partial blocks, tenant salts, collision odds, radix tree vs hash blocks, and Kimi K3's hybrid prefix cache. R-XIII.3, R-XIII.5.

labels.hashes: illustrative digests (same chain structure as vLLM, different serialization)
labels.hash_serialization: SHA-256 over: parent digest (32 bytes) | number of tokens (uint32 big-endian) | token IDs (uint32 big-endian each) | extra keys as canonical JSON (sorted keys, no spaces)
labels.segment_lengths: hypothetical (class C), chosen for this demo

blocks.result: partial block: never hashed, never cached

lookup.max_cache_hit_tokens_rule: num_tokens - 1 (the last prompt token is always recomputed for its logits)
lookup.later_blocks: all miss: each hash chains its parent, so a miss at one block means a miss for every later block

straddling_block.why: its hash covers all 16 token IDs plus the parent hash; the D tokens differ from the C tokens

trtllm_partial_reuse_comparison.note: TRT-LLM copies the matched tokens of a partially matched block into a new block; vLLM recomputes the whole block

full_hit_edge_cases.case: a cached prompt whose length is a multiple of the block size
full_hit_edge_cases.why: only num_tokens - 1 tokens may hit and hits are whole blocks, so a whole block is recomputed

tenant_isolation.rule: cache_salt is added to the extra keys of block 0 only; every later block chains block 0
tenant_isolation.radix_equivalent: SGLang namespaces the child key by (extra_key, cache_salt), so salted requests live in disjoint subtrees

stated_block_count.derivation: daily_active_users x requests_per_dau_per_day x mean_prompt_tokens / block_size x 365 days (hypothetical traffic; every full block of every prompt for one year, an overestimate because one pool holds far fewer)

xxhash_128.note: non-cryptographic: an attacker can search for colliding blocks offline, which is why vLLM seeds it randomly per process and warns about multi-tenant use

radix_timeline.event: R1 arrives: radix match 0 tokens, inserts 40
R2 arrives: radix match 27 tokens, inserts 12
R1 finishes: lock_ref released on its path
R3 arrives: radix match 19 tokens, inserts 15

notes: R2's match ends inside R1's edge, so the edge is split into a shared node and R1's remainder
R3's match ends inside the shared node, so it is split again
a split node inherits the lock_ref of the node it was cut from
hash blocks only hit whole 16-token blocks; the radix tree hits every matching token

why_kda_needs_a_checkpoint: MLA layers keep K/V for every token, so any hash-block boundary can be reused by reading the first B tokens' KV
KDA layers keep one fixed-size recurrent state S_t (plus the short-conv tail) that is overwritten at every token
to resume at B = 2560 the KDA layers need S_2560 exactly; it cannot be rebuilt from the cached MLA KV
so the state is saved (a checkpoint) at selected hash endpoints; a hit is cut back to the last endpoint that has one

simplifications: Radix tree: only prompt tokens are inserted (SGLang also inserts generated tokens when a request finishes).
Radix tree: KV slot indices come from a counter, not from SGLang's token-to-KV pool allocator.
Radix tree: no eviction is exercised.
Hash blocks: one KV-cache group; no LoRA, multimodal or prompt-embedding extra keys.
K3 checkpoint bytes are the fixed per-sequence KDA state at TP=1 (fp32 recurrent + bf16 conv), and the per-rank value assumes TP=8 sharding by head.
